title: Multiplication language is in log space
statement: Let $L$ be the language of bit strings of the form $\langle \operatorname{bits}(a),\langle \operatorname{bits}(b),\operatorname{bits}(ab)\rangle\rangle$, where $a,b$ are nonnegative integers, $\operatorname{bits}(n)$ is the bit string of $n$, and $\langle x,y\rangle$ doubles each bit of $x$, appends the separator $01$, and then appends $y$. Then $L$ is decidable by a finite-state, deterministic multi-tape Turing machine using at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells on inputs of length $n$, for some nonnegative integer constant $c$.
